candidates: When importing from a subpath of an external package (e.g., `package/subpath`), verify that the subpath is declared in the package's `exports` field before committing the import; an undeclared subpath causes a runtime module-resolution failure regardless of whether TypeScript compiles cleanly.

Avoid unnecessary variable assignments: reference an already-computed variable instead of re-deriving the same value elsewhere in the same scope, and inline single-use local variables when the expression is self-explanatory and the variable name adds no clarity.

When resolving file paths to internal storybook modules at runtime (in builders, plugins, or utilities), use `fileURLToPath(import.meta.resolve('storybook/internal/<export-name>'))` with the name declared in `code/core/package.json` exports rather than constructing paths directly into the `dist` directory; the package-export form is stable across rebuild cycles and safe under all package managers.
Module-level constants (values that never change and are not function parameters) should be named in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (e.g., `ENTRY_PATH`, `MAX_RETRIES`) rather than camelCase.

In build scripts and prebuild files, catch blocks must rethrow the error (or use `throw`) rather than only logging it with `console.error(error)`; swallowing the error discards the stack trace and makes the root cause invisible to CI and local debugging.

When a prebuild or code-generation script needs to invoke logic from another module, prefer exporting a named function and importing it statically rather than dynamically importing the module by file path; static imports are simpler, provide full TypeScript type-checking, and avoid the indirection of runtime file-path construction.

Exported utility functions that are consumed by packages outside their own module (e.g., called by builders or framework integrations) should include a JSDoc comment that names those consumers, so future readers can quickly understand the function's call sites without grepping the monorepo.

In `scripts/build/utils/generate-bundle.ts`, whenever an entry is added to the `external` array, include an inline comment identifying which package or feature requires the externalization and explaining why it is safe (e.g., which import paths are never actually invoked at runtime).
